summary: Implemented cross-LAN firewall via Ansible from control node4: node1 (VyOS) routes lan-a (10.50.1.0/24, node2) and lan-b (10.50.2.0/24, node3), with a forward-filter policy that allows only node2->node3 TCP/5432 (plus established/related) and drops all other cross-LAN traffic. Verified end-to-end (ICMP blocked, TCP/22 blocked, TCP/5432 succeeds) both before and after restarting all four managed nodes one at a time, with saved VyOS config and NetworkManager/firewalld state confirmed to persist across reboot.
actions_performed: Mapped topology via temporary IP/ping tests: node1 eth1<->node2 eth1 (lan-a), node1 eth2<->node3 eth1 (lan-b)
Wired passwordless cluster SSH key onto node4 (control node) and into VyOS's own persistent public-keys config on node1, plus authorized_keys on node2/node3

Diagnosed a VyOS non-interactive SSH config-session bug (missing /etc/default/vyatta env vars and root:root-owned active-config subdirectories blocking the vyos user) and worked around it using sudo-elevated bash + script-template

Wrote an Ansible project (~/ansible-lan-fw on node4): inventory.ini and playbook.yml configuring VyOS interface addresses, a forward-filter policy (default-drop, established/related allow, node2->node3 tcp/5432 allow), static LAN IPs + cross-LAN static routes on node2/node3 via nmcli, and a firewalld port opening on node3

Fixed incorrect VyOS firewall syntax ('state established enable' -> 'state established') found by inspecting the live nft ruleset, which showed the original rule was an unconditional accept instead of a state match
Verified firewall behavior with a real TCP/5432 listener on node3: ping blocked, TCP/22 blocked, TCP/5432 succeeds, in both directions

Captured a pre-restart baseline (boot_id, addressing, firewall/nft state) on all 4 nodes, then restarted each one at a time via native reboot, polled until exec returned, and confirmed a changed boot_id plus full recovery of VyOS saved config/firewall, NetworkManager static IP/routes, firewalld port, and Ansible tooling

Found and fixed a persistence gap where node1's live-boot overlay regenerates authorized_keys from VyOS config on boot, discarding a manually-appended key; re-added the SSH key through 'set system login user vyos authentication public-keys' so it survives reboot, then re-ran the playbook and re-verified end-to-end connectivity

evidence.requirement: node2 can reach node3 on TCP/5432, all other cross-LAN traffic rejected
evidence.summary: nft ruleset and live tests from node2 show ICMP and TCP/22 blocked while TCP/5432 to node3 succeeds with a real HTTP response; node3->node2 traffic also blocked
ansible-playbook run from node4 (control node) against inventory covering node1 (VyOS), node2, node3, applying interface/firewall config and LAN host addressing/routes/firewalld

evidence.requirement: node1 restart baseline, ack, changed boot identity, recovery
evidence.summary: Captured boot_id/nft/addressing baseline, issued shutdown -r now, polled until exec returned with a new boot_id, and confirmed eth1/eth2 addressing and forward-filter rules persisted from saved config

evidence.requirement: node2 restart baseline, ack, changed boot identity, recovery
evidence.summary: Captured boot_id/addressing baseline, issued reboot, polled until exec returned with a new boot_id, confirmed eth1 static IP and static route to lan-b persisted

evidence.requirement: node3 restart baseline, ack, changed boot identity, recovery
evidence.summary: Captured boot_id/addressing/firewalld baseline, issued reboot, polled until exec returned with a new boot_id, confirmed eth1 static IP, static route to lan-a, and firewalld port 5432 persisted

evidence.requirement: node4 restart baseline, ack, changed boot identity, recovery
evidence.summary: Captured boot_id/workspace baseline on control node, issued reboot, polled until exec returned with a new boot_id, confirmed ansible-lan-fw workspace and ansible-playbook tooling intact; discovered node1 lost the manually-added SSH key on its own reboot, fixed it via persistent VyOS config, and successfully re-ran the playbook end-to-end

evidence.requirement: End-to-end connectivity re-verified after full restart cycle
evidence.summary: Post-reboot re-test: TCP/5432 from node2 to node3 returns HTTP 200, ICMP and TCP/22 blocked; test listener cleaned up and no stale VyOS config sessions remain
